topic.name: The Average Rate of Change of a Function over a Varying Interval

question.text: A function $f(x) = 4x-\dfrac6x$ is defined on an interval $[a,6]$, where $a$ is a negative parameter. Calculate $a$ such that the average rate of change over $[a,6]$ is equal to $3.$
question.explanation: Let's calculate the average rate of change of $f(x)$ over the interval $[a,6]$: \begin{align*} \dfrac{\Delta f}{\Delta x} & = \dfrac { f(b) - f(a)}{b-a} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac {\left(4(6)-\dfrac66\right)-\left(4(a)-\dfrac6a\right) }{6 - a}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac {23-4a+\dfrac6a} {6-a}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac {23-4a+\dfrac6a} {6-a} \cdot \dfrac{a}{a}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac {23a-4a^2+6} {a(6-a)}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac {6+23a-4a^2} {a(6-a)}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac {(6-a)(1+4a)} {a(6-a)}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\cancel{(6-a)}(1+4a)} {a\cancel{(6-a)}}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1+4a}{a} \end{align*} We want $\dfrac{\Delta f}{\Delta x}$ be equal to $3$, so \begin{align*} \dfrac{1+4a}{a} & = 3\\[5pt] 1+4a & = 3a\\[5pt] a & = -1. \end{align*} Since $a< 0$, we conclude that $a = -1$ and the interval is $[-1,6].$

example.title: Determining the Interval Over Which the Average Rate of Change of a Function is a Given Number

question.text: Find the average rate of change of the function $y = -5x$ over the interval $x\in[-1,-1+h]$, where $h>0$ is a parameter.
question.explanation:
Let $f(x)=-5x.$ Notice that we are given the length $h$ of the interval, so we use \[ \dfrac{\Delta y}{\Delta x} = \dfrac{f(a+h) - f(a)}{h}, \] with $a=-1.$ Substituting into the formula gives

\begin{align*} \require{cancel} \dfrac{\Delta y}{\Delta x} &= \dfrac{f(a+h) - f(a)}{h}\\[2pt] &= \dfrac{-5(-1+h) - (-5)(-1)}{h}\\[2pt] &= \dfrac{ 5-5h-5}{h}\\[2pt] &= \dfrac{-5h}{h}\\[2pt] &= -5. \end{align*}

example.title: Calculating the Average Rate of Change Over a Varying Interval where the Parameter Represents Distance

question.text: Find the average rate of change of the function $y = -2x$ over the interval $x\in[4,4+h]$, where $h>0$ is a parameter.
question.explanation:
Let $f(x)=-2x.$ Notice that we are given the length $h$ of the interval, so we use \[ \dfrac{\Delta y}{\Delta x} = \dfrac{f(a+h) - f(a)}{h}, \] with $a=4.$ Substituting into the formula gives \[ \begin{align*} \require{cancel} \dfrac{\Delta y}{\Delta x} &= \dfrac{f(4+h) - f(4)}{h}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{-2(4+h) - (-2)(4)}{h}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{-8-2h+8}{h}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{-2\cancel{h}}{\cancel{h}}\\[5pt] &= -2. \end{align*} \]

So, the average rate of change is $\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-2}.$
